title: Search for a document
description: Find a filed document by typing a word from it, open the page, zoom, and jump to a word on the page. Explains why every page is searchable and what the filters are for.

steps.narration: Once documents are filed you rarely need the folders at all. Here's how to find any document in seconds, just by typing something that's printed on it.
steps.caption: Find any document in seconds

steps.narration: Click Search in the side bar.
steps.caption: 1. Click Search

steps.narration: Type anything printed on the document — a supplier name, a reference number, even an amount. Every word on every page was read when it was filed, so it's all searchable.
steps.caption: 2. Type a word from the document

steps.narration: Every matching document is listed on the left, with its sender, type and date.
steps.caption: Matches appear on the left

steps.narration: Click one, and the page appears on the right.
steps.caption: 4. Click a result

steps.narration: That's the actual scanned page, exactly as it was filed — no digging through folders.
steps.caption: The filed page, as scanned

steps.narration: Zoom in to read the small print.
steps.caption: 5. Zoom in

steps.narration: To jump straight to a word on the page — an amount, a part number — type it into the find box.
steps.caption: 6. Find a word on the page

steps.narration: Each match is highlighted on the page, and Next steps through them.
steps.caption: 7. Next match

steps.narration: When a word alone isn't enough, narrow it down with the filters along the top: a date range, an amount, or the document type.
steps.caption: Filters: date range · amount · type

steps.narration: That's Search. Every word on every page, the moment a document is filed.
steps.caption: Every word, every page, searchable
